main_text.p: propter regulã, Legitimè res vendita & tradita emptoris esto. Quæsitum est enim, le-gitimé ne vendita res esset: quod negatur. Ex quo intelligi debet, non contraCtum vẽditionis, sed σωναλλαγμα[?], id est, permutationem & æqualitatem rei cum precio dominium trãsferre. Item Sextianæ causæ status definitionis est. Lex est: Qui vim publicè fecerit, pœnas luito. P. Sextius, ut lex de Cicerone revocãdo perferri posset, nec vi à Clodianis impediretur, præsidium armatorum ho-minum habuit: cumque iis etiã pugnauit. Accusatur à M. Al-

page.notes: Right margin: two handwritten annotations (one beside "Sextianæ", one beside "Cicerone") are manuscript ink, not printed, so they are omitted. Greek "σωναλλαγμα" is printed in italic and is read here with some doubt; the initial letter may be a ligature for συ. Spelling in the Latin has been normalised for u/v, i/j and long s as instructed. "contraCtum" and "pugnauit" are kept as printed. Page ends mid-sentence; the continuation is on the next page.
